statement: 100 numbers were written around a circle. The sum of the 100 numbers is equal to 100 and the sum of any six consecutive numbers is always less than or equal to 6. The first number is 6. Find all the numbers.
Decide if there exists a 10-digit number such that rearranging its digits in 10,000 ways yields 10,000 different numbers that are all multiples of 7.

The non-regular hexagon \(ABCDEF\) is inscribed in a circle of center \(O\) with \(AB = CD = EF\). Diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(M\), diagonals \(CE\) and \(DF\) intersect at \(N\), and diagonals \(AE\) and \(BF\) intersect at \(K\). Show that the altitudes of triangle \(MNK\) intersect at \(O\).

Let \(ABCD\) be a parallelogram with center \(O\) such that \(\angle BAD < 90^\circ\) and \(\angle AOB > 90^\circ\). Consider points \(A_1\) and \(B_1\) on rays \(OA\) and \(OB\) respectively, such that \(A_1B_1 \parallel AB\) and \(\angle A_1B_1C = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle ABC\). Prove that \(A_1D \perp B_1C\).

Determine all positive real numbers \(x\) for which
\[\lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{1996x} \rfloor = 1996\]
is satisfied, where \(\lfloor \cdot \rfloor\) denotes the integer part.

In a tennis tournament with 10 players, everyone plays against everyone else exactly once. If player \(i\) beats player \(j\), then the total number of matches \(i\) lost plus the total number of matches \(j\) won is greater than or equal to 8. Three players \(i, j, k\) form an atypical trio if \(i\) beat \(j\), \(j\) beat \(k\), and \(k\) beat \(i\). Prove that there are exactly 40 atypical trios in the tournament.
